Are you up to the challenge?

- Gain hands-on mentoring and coaching from the industry’s top IT professionals
- Connect with peers from across the country
- Find summer internship and post-grad opportunities

- Travel reimbursement available up to $200 per person

title: Travel Fund | Matthew & Margarethe Mashikian Innovation & Entrepreneurship Hub | College of Engineering | University of Connecticut
text:
Travel Fund | Matthew & Margarethe Mashikian Innovation & Entrepreneurship Hub | College of Engineering | University of Connecticut

 E-Mail : engr-ehub@uconn.edu 

# Travel Fund

The eHub’s Travel Fund helps students, postdocs, and researchers attend external pitch competitions to showcase their tech-enabled innovations. The fund provides up to $750 per competition to cover travel, lodging, and registration costs. By supporting attendance at these events, we aim to help innovators refine their pitches, gain exposure, and build connections with investors, mentors, and collaborators.

## Fund Details

- Eligibility: Students, postdocs, and researchers involved in technology-driven innovations.
- Pitch Acceptance Requirement: Applicants must be confirmed to pitch at the event, and proof of acceptance (e.g., confirmation email or letter) is required as part of the application.
- Award Amount: Up to $750 per event.
- Use of Funds: Travel, lodging, registration fees, and other event-related expenses.
- Expectations: Recipients are expected to submit a short report summarizing their experience, key learnings, and outcomes.

## Application Process

Applications are accepted on a rolling basis, but must be submitted at least 6 weeks before the event to allow time for review and funding approval. Early submissions are encouraged.

## Contact Us

For questions or more information, email Dr. Leila Daneshmandi: leila.daneshmandi@uconn.edu.

# Summer Fellows Grants

February 17, 2025· by Harj Taggar

This summer, YC will be giving grants to college students to work on their own technical projects. We’re calling these the Summer Fellows Grants. We hope this will encourage the smartest students to indulge their intellectual curiosity this summer instead of doing intern grunt work. Now is the best time ever to do this — AI models keep pushing the limits of what's possible to build, and AI tools are rapidly making programmers more productive. The returns from spending a summer building things at the edge of your programming ability have never been higher.

The grants will be $20,000 in cash and $90,000 in compute credits from Amazon AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google GCP. Summer Fellows will also be invited to YC's AI Startup School June 16 - 17, and we’ll also hold some special events:

- June 15: Kickoff dinner with the other Fellows and guests
- June 18 - 20: We’ll host you to co-work from the YC office.
- Aug 20 - 22: Co-working again from the YC office.
- Aug 22: Present what you’ve built to everyone at Demo Day.

We’re most interested in funding technical projects using AI in new ways, but we’re happy to fund anything that smart programmers find interesting. We’re not expecting the projects to be commercial or make money, though it’d be fine if they did.

## ATC 2026 Student Scholarships and Travel Grants

ATC 2026 offers a limited number of grants to help full-time undergraduate and graduate students attend the conference in Hong Kong. Students may apply whether or not they are presenting work.

Funding is competitive and may cover conference registration and part of reasonable travel and accommodation expenses. Awards may not cover all requested costs.

### Eligibility

Applicants must:

- be enrolled full-time at an accredited institution;
- study computer science, computer engineering, or a related field;
- attend ATC 2026 in person if selected; and
- disclose all confirmed or pending funding for the trip.

Postdoctoral researchers are also eligible.

### Application Materials

Please submit:

- the completed application form;
- a CV of no more than two pages;
- proof of current full-time student status.

Applications will be evaluated based on financial need, relevance to ATC, expected benefit from attending, available institutional support, and contributions to broad participation.

title: The 2026 ACM SIGMOD/PODS Conference: Bengaluru, India: Student Travel Grants
text:
The 2026 ACM SIGMOD/PODS Conference: Bengaluru, India: Student Travel Grants

# SIGMOD 2026 Student Travel Grants

Thanks to the generous support from SIGMOD and other sponsors including the National Science Foundation, we will provide scholarship awards to selected students attending the SIGMOD/PODS conference. The scholarships will include financial support for traveling. 

Each awardee will receive a stipend to partially cover the expense to attend the conference. The amount will be determined based on the availability of funds and the number of granted stipends. Awardees are expected to register to the main conference and will have to make their own arrangements for travel and accommodation. 

## Eligibility

Applicants need to be a full-time student (undergraduate,graduate or PhD). 

Applicants are eligible to apply for the SIGMOD travel award even if they have submissions under consideration at other events at SIGMOD, such as the Undergraduate Research Program, or the New Researcher Symposium. However, an applicant cannot receive more than one travel award in total. 

Applicants do not need to have an accepted paper to be eligible. However, students who are primary authors of an accepted paper in the main conference or the workshops are especially encouraged to apply. Junior students without papers accepted for publication at SIGMOD/PODS, but involved in research closely related to the topics of the conference are also encouraged to apply.
